packet.headline_seed: Lamine Yamal celebrates World Cup win with little brother who charmed fans
packet.description_seed: The three-year-old brother of Yamal has been hailed one of Spain's World Cup breakout stars by fans

what: Lamine Yamal celebrates World Cup win with little brother who charmed fans

clean_source_blocks.text: Spanish footballer Lamine Yamal may have lifted the World Cup but it is his little brother Kenye who appears to have stolen the spotlight. The three-year-old quickly become an internet sensation after footage of his exuberant celebrations following Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina spread across social media on Sunday. While the footballer, just 19 himself, continued his rise by helping Spain achieve football's biggest prize, attention swiftly turned to his younger brother's joyful reactions from the sidelines. From sticking out his tongue on the big screen to wildly cheering on his older brother, Kenye has been hailed by fans as one of the unexpected breakout stars of the 2026 tournament. Lamine Yamal's little brother steals the show at full time
The three-year-old brother of Yamal has been hailed one of Spain's World Cup breakout stars by fans

Spain triumphed in a battle of endurance, beating Argentina with a goal in the 106th minute at the New York New Jersey Stadium. The team's second World Cup win has led to Lamine Yamal becoming the youngest player ever to win both the European Championship and the World Cup. His younger brother Kenye has become a regular fixture both on and off the pitch - often featuring in Lamine Yamal's TikToks and charming fans from around the world. The three-year-old, who appears keen to follow in his big brother's footsteps, is the son of Lamine Yamal's mother Sheila Ebana. Speaking about Kenye, Lamine Yamal previously told outlets: "I'm moved when I see my little brother this happy, as well as seeing my mum and friends living the life they always dreamed of.

Spain's Lamine Yamal is tipped to take the world by storm in the coming years, but not before his younger brother steals the show. Yamal won the World Cup on Sunday and played all 120 minutes in the 1-0 victory over Argentina. The 19-year-old's half-brother Keyne charmed audiences around the world with his enthusiastic celebrations and the three-year-old was at it again at MetLife Stadium. He poked his tongue out after seeing himself on the big screen as he fulfilled his promise to his footballer sibling. Yamal said after lifting the trophy: "I was at physio and he called me, using my mum's phone, and told me that he was going to stick his tongue out tomorrow. So that's why when I saw him on the screen, it really made me laugh."

[Lähde: Yahoo Sports | URL: https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/watch-lamine-yamal-little-brother-074720270.html]
Spain's Lamine Yamal is tipped to take the world by storm in the coming years, but not before his younger brother steals the show.

Yamal won the World Cup on Sunday and played all 120 minutes in the 1-0 victory over Argentina.

The 19-year-old's half-brother Keyne charmed audiences around the world with his enthusiastic celebrations and the three-year-old was at it again at MetLife Stadium. He poked his tongue out after seeing himself on the big screen as he fulfilled his promise to his footballer sibling.

Yamal said after lifting the trophy: "I was at physio and he called me, using my mum's phone, and told me that he was going to stick his tongue out tomorrow. So that's why when I saw him on the screen, it really made me laugh."

Dressed in a Spain jersey with his name on the back, Keyne stormed around the pitch as he looked to celebrate. Yamal lifted his brother into the air after sharing a hug and put a "Lamine" baseball hat on his head.

Keyne was pictured dancing near a giant replica of the World Cup trophy and grabbed the real thing, too. He later could be seen bumping fists with Yamal and holding a football, while a New Jersey state trooper shared his hat with the little fan.

The toddler, dubbed "the star of the World Cup" in Spain, featured regularly at the tournament. He celebrated Spain's quarter-final win over Belgium with real gusto and also reacted with joy at seeing himself on the big screen.

"This time around, the biggest sensation of the competition isn't an athlete, the goals, or even the trophy itself," Hola! – Spain's version of Hello! magazine – has said previously. "It's Keyne, Lamine Yamal's three-year-old brother, who's taking the tournament by storm with his hilarious moments."

Keyne was born in September 2022 and is the son of Yamal's mother, Sheila Ebana. He was also a feature of Euro 2024 (below), when Spain defeated England in the final in Germany.

"I'm moved when I see my little brother this happy, as well as seeing my mum and friends living the life they always dreamed of," Yamal said previously. "My little brother means everything to me. I am in love with him; it feels like he is my son."

payload.title: Lamine Yamal juhli maailmanmestaruutta – kolmivuotias pikkuveli hurmasi fanit
payload.summary: Espanja voitti Argentiinan jalkapallon MM-finaalissa 1–0. Mestaruusjuhlissa huomio kiinnittyi myös Lamine Yamalin kolmivuotiaaseen pikkuveljeen Kenyeen ja tämän riemukkaisiin eleisiin.
payload.content:
Espanjan 19-vuotias jalkapalloilija Lamine Yamal juhli sunnuntaina maailmanmestaruutta, kun Espanja voitti Argentiinan 1–0 pitkään venyneessä MM-finaalissa. Yamal pelasi ottelun kaikki 120 minuuttia, mutta ratkaisuhetkien jälkeen osa huomiosta siirtyi hänen kolmivuotiaaseen pikkuveljeensä Kenyeen. Lapsen innostuneet reaktiot katsomossa ja kentän laidalla levisivät nopeasti sosiaalisessa mediassa. Huomio kääntyi varsinkin hänen riemukkaaseen kannustukseensa ja eleeseensä stadionin suurella näytöllä.

Finaali ratkesi vasta jatkoajalla, kun Espanja teki voittomaalin 106. minuutilla New York New Jersey Stadiumilla. Ratkaisu päätti pitkän kestävyyskamppailun jatkoajan jälkimmäisellä puoliskolla. Tulos toi maalle sen historian toisen jalkapallon maailmanmestaruuden. Yamalin henkilökohtainen saavutus oli samalla historiallinen: hänestä tuli nuorin pelaaja, joka on voittanut sekä Euroopan mestaruuden että maailmanmestaruuden. Voitto jatkoi hänen nopeaa nousuaan lajin huipulle.

## Kenyen ele nauratti Yamalia

Kenye kannusti veljeään äänekkäästi ja työnsi kielensä ulos huomattuaan itsensä stadionin suurella näytöllä. Yamal kertoi pokaalin nostamisen jälkeen, että pikkuveli oli soittanut hänelle äitinsä puhelimella tämän ollessa fysioterapiassa. Kolmivuotias oli luvannut puhelussa näyttää seuraavana päivänä kieltä. Kun hän toteutti lupauksensa näytöllä, tilanne sai Yamalin nauramaan kesken mestaruusjuhlien.

Hetkestä kuvatut videot ja muut juhlakohtaukset levisivät sunnuntaina verkossa. Fanit nostivat Kenyen yhdeksi Espanjan vuoden 2026 MM-turnauksen odottamattomista tähdistä. Kolmivuotiaan riemu näkyi sekä äänekkäänä kannustuksena että leikkisänä kielen näyttämisenä. Näin mestaruuspokaalia nostaneen Yamalin rinnalle nousi toinenkin saman perheen huomionkohde.

## Pikkuveli on tuttu Yamalin seuraajille

Kenye ei ollut Yamalin seuraajille täysin uusi kasvo. Hän on esiintynyt usein isoveljensä TikTok-videoilla ja ollut tämän mukana sekä kentällä että sen ulkopuolella. Kolmivuotias on Yamalin äidin Sheila Ebanan poika. Hänen on myös kuvattu olevan innokas seuraamaan isoveljensä jalanjälkiä. Yhteiset esiintymiset ovat tehneet hänestä tutun monille jalkapalloilijan seuraajille jo ennen MM-finaalin laajalle levinneitä juhlakuvia.

Yamal on aiemmin kertonut liikuttuvansa nähdessään pikkuveljensä näin iloisena. Samassa yhteydessä hän puhui myös siitä, miltä tuntuu nähdä äitinsä ja ystäviensä elävän elämää, josta nämä olivat unelmoineet. Sunnuntain finaalissa perheen ilo näkyi konkreettisesti: Yamal saavutti jalkapallon suurimman palkinnon, ja Kenyen reaktiot jäivät yhdeksi Espanjan toisen maailmanmestaruuden näkyvistä juhlahetkistä.
summary_bullets: Espanja voitti Argentiinan MM-finaalissa 1–0 jatkoajalla syntyneellä maalilla.
Lamine Yamalista tuli nuorin sekä Euroopan mestaruuden että maailmanmestaruuden voittanut pelaaja.
Yamalin kolmivuotias pikkuveli Kenye herätti huomiota riemukkaalla juhlimisellaan.
payload.journalist_note: Pikkuveljen nimi kirjoitettiin aineistossa kahdella tavalla. Artikkelissa käytetään valitun pääaineiston kirjoitusasua Kenye; nimi on syytä tarkistaa ennen julkaisua.

article.source_text:
Spanish footballer Lamine Yamal may have lifted the World Cup but it is his little brother Kenye who appears to have stolen the spotlight. The three-year-old quickly become an internet sensation after footage of his exuberant celebrations following Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina spread across social media on Sunday. While the footballer, just 19 himself, continued his rise by helping Spain achieve football's biggest prize, attention swiftly turned to his younger brother's joyful reactions from the sidelines. From sticking out his tongue on the big screen to wildly cheering on his older brother, Kenye has been hailed by fans as one of the unexpected breakout stars of the 2026 tournament. Lamine Yamal's little brother steals the show at full time

The three-year-old brother of Yamal has been hailed one of Spain's World Cup breakout stars by fans

Spain triumphed in a battle of endurance, beating Argentina with a goal in the 106th minute at the New York New Jersey Stadium. The team's second World Cup win has led to Lamine Yamal becoming the youngest player ever to win both the European Championship and the World Cup. His younger brother Kenye has become a regular fixture both on and off the pitch - often featuring in Lamine Yamal's TikToks and charming fans from around the world. The three-year-old, who appears keen to follow in his big brother's footsteps, is the son of Lamine Yamal's mother Sheila Ebana. Speaking about Kenye, Lamine Yamal previously told outlets: "I'm moved when I see my little brother this happy, as well as seeing my mum and friends living the life they always dreamed of.

Spain's Lamine Yamal is tipped to take the world by storm in the coming years, but not before his younger brother steals the show. Yamal won the World Cup on Sunday and played all 120 minutes in the 1-0 victory over Argentina. The 19-year-old's half-brother Keyne charmed audiences around the world with his enthusiastic celebrations and the three-year-old was at it again at MetLife Stadium. He poked his tongue out after seeing himself on the big screen as he fulfilled his promise to his footballer sibling. Yamal said after lifting the trophy: "I was at physio and he called me, using my mum's phone, and told me that he was going to stick his tongue out tomorrow. So that's why when I saw him on the screen, it really made me laugh."
